q: Morning mists rise off a small tributary south of Angers and burn away by midday, autumn after autumn. Which wine style does that pattern make possible?
exp: Damp nights let noble rot establish and dry afternoons stop it turning grey and destructive. The Layon valley is one of the few places in France where that rhythm is reliable.

q: Grand Cru rank appears on exactly one Loire label. Which appellation carries it?
exp: A tiny south-facing amphitheatre of schist above the Layon, sheltered from the north and reliably misted at dawn. Yields are the lowest of any Loire appellation.

q: Within the commune of Thouarce, a run of steep schist slopes carries its own sweet-wine appellation inside the wider Layon zone. Which?
exp: Three south-facing slopes above the river, worked for botrytised and raisined Chenin. It is the largest of the Layon's separately named sweet appellations and among the longest-lived.

q: A smaller tributary runs south of Angers between the Loire and the Layon, and its schist slopes make sweet Chenin in a lighter, earlier-drinking register than the celebrated valley to the south-west. Which appellation sits there?
exp: The Aubance runs a few kilometres north-east of the Layon over the same dark rock, but its slopes are gentler and noble rot arrives less reliably. The wines are usually made in a lighter style and drunk within a decade, and the appellation stays far less known than its bigger neighbour.

q: Noble rot does not form in every autumn, yet sweet wine is still made. Which vineyard route concentrates the sugar instead?
opts: Passerillage, the fruit raisining on the vine
Fortification of the must with grape spirit
Freezing the fruit in the winery to draw off water
Chaptalisation of the must before fermentation
exp: Left hanging into a dry autumn, the berry loses water through its skin and the sugar concentrates without any fungus. The result is purer and more apricot-like, with less of the honeyed botrytis note.

q: A fifty-year-old Quarts de Chaume still tastes fresh rather than cloying. Which quality of the grape explains that?
opts: The new oak it was raised in
exp: Sugar without acid tastes flabby within a decade. Chenin holds enough acidity to carry two hundred grams of residual sugar and still finish clean, which is why these wines outlive most Sauternes drinkers expect them to.

q: On the right bank east of Tours, a single appellation makes dry, off-dry, sweet and sparkling wine from one grape. Which is it?
exp: Chenin's acidity lets a grower choose the style after seeing what the year delivers. The tuffeau slope above the river is honeycombed with cellars cut into the rock.

q: Hemmed between the Loire and the Cher on the left bank, which appellation won independence from its more famous neighbour in 1938?
exp: Sandier soils over the tuffeau give a slightly quicker, more open style. The same range of dry through sweet and sparkling is made, and the wines are almost always the better value of the pair.

q: A guest wants a Vouvray with clear sweetness on the palate but stops well short of a dessert wine. Which label term sends you to the right bottle?
exp: Sec is dry and moelleux is frankly sweet, with doux sweeter again. Demi-sec sits between them, carrying enough sugar to read as off-dry while staying a wine for the table rather than the dessert course.

q: A cold, wet summer leaves the fruit at modest ripeness with searing acidity. What will a Vouvray producer make from it?
opts: Dry still wine and sparkling wine
exp: High acid and low sugar is exactly the profile a base wine wants, so poor years go to the sparkling cuvee. Sweet wine is only attempted when the autumn delivers rot or raisining.

q: A sommelier is asked for Loire bubbles that carry a single village name rather than the valley-wide Cremant. Which appellation can supply them?
exp: Sparkling wine is written into the rules of Vouvray and Montlouis, as it is at Saumur and in Anjou, so the village name carries the fizz on its own label. Sancerre, Muscadet and Chinon have no sparkling category of their own. Sancerre and Muscadet also lie outside the Cremant de Loire zone, so a grower there who wants bubbles has to leave appellation wine altogether, while a Chinon grower at least sits inside that zone and can declassify into Cremant de Loire.

q: Two levels of fizz are permitted in Vouvray and Montlouis, and the gentler one carries markedly lower pressure. Which term marks it?
exp: Petillant is softly frothing rather than fully sparkling, and is the older local style. Tranquille simply means still, so it marks the absence of any bubble at all.

q: Local growers call it Breton, a name with no connection to Brittany at all. Which variety?
exp: The origin of the name is disputed: it appears in Rabelais in 1534, well before the abbot Breton usually credited with it, and one account ties it instead to vines arriving through a Breton port. It buds and ripens early, which is what lets it work this far north.

q: Vines along the Vienne, just above its confluence with the Loire, feed which red appellation?
exp: The town sits under a vast medieval fortress on the Vienne. Bourgueil and Saint-Nicolas lie on the opposite bank of the Loire a short distance downstream.

q: Among Chinon, Bourgueil and Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil, only one may also bottle a white wine. Which, and from what grape?
exp: Chinon Blanc is a small but genuine part of the appellation, and there is a Chinon rose as well. The two Bourgueil appellations are restricted to red and rose only.

q: Two soil types split the reds of Chinon: light sand and gravel terraces beside the river, and limestone slopes above them. What does that difference produce?
opts: White wine from the terraces and red wine from the slopes
Sweet wine from the terraces and dry wine from the slopes
Early-drinking wine from the terraces and ageworthy wine from the slopes
Firm, ageworthy wine from the terraces and light, fruity wine from the slopes
exp: Free-draining sand gives a supple wine for drinking within a few years. The tuffeau slopes hold more water and give structure, and those are the bottlings worth cellaring.
